owner: RI-CAM01 §A–§E, RI-CAM02 §A–§E, RI-CAM03 §B–§G, RI-CAM05 §A–§F, RI-CAM06 §A–§I. Seam S18.
note: Every constant the camera rig uses, transcribed from the reference items so a critic can diff the DECLARATION (this file) against the OBSERVATION (the camera trace channel) without reading JavaScript — HARNESS.md §5 and §7 rule 4. No number below is computed at runtime from another number in a way that could drift: the derived table at the bottom is recomputed by the code at boot and asserted against these cells.

rig.pivot_height_is_above: the character's GROUND CONTACT (feet), not the root

pivot_follow.horizontal: RIGID. pivot.xz == controller.xz every frame. No spring, no lag, no lead.

spring_arm.cast_origin: the pivot, never the current camera position

penetration_guard._source: RI-CAM01 §C step 7 — 'the rate limit is a smoothing device, never a correctness device'
penetration_guard.guard_radius_rationale: The near-plane corner of a 50° / 16:9 / 0.10 m frustum lies 0.1383 m from the camera origin. A guard sphere strictly larger than that makes `clip_through == false` a STRUCTURAL property of an overlap-free camera sphere rather than a test that happens to pass.
penetration_guard.declared_deviation: RI-CAM05 §F states the 0.90 m arm floor holds 'on every frame of every state, forever'. RI-CAM01 §C step 7 places the penetration guard AFTER the 0.90 m clamp of step 5 and says correctness wins. Those two lines are over-determined the moment a character with a 0.55 m collision radius puts its back flat against a wall: the obstruction is then 0.55 m from the pivot, a 0.90 m arm is 0.35 m inside the rock, and `clip_through` — an automatic fail with weight 25 — becomes true. This build resolves it in the corpus's own stated order: the 0.90 m floor governs, the guard overrides it when and only when the near-plane volume would be inside solid geometry, and every such frame is flagged `arm_penetration_guard: true` (a flag RI-CAM01 M4 already anticipates). The floor is never breached on any authored interior or any of the three worst-geometry routes, because those obey RI-CAM05 §D's architecture minimums — which is the corpus's own remedy: the fix for a jammed camera is a wider corridor.

pitch_clamp.behaviour_at_bound: saturates: no overshoot, no bounce, no easing back, no rubber band

movement.facing_never_assigned: There is no frame on which facing := facing_target. The only instant facing changes in the game are the attack frame-1 snap and the unlocked roll frame-1 snap.

auto_recentre.disengage: IMMEDIATE, same frame, on look input / sprint release / speed drop / lock-on / committed state / leaving grounded

lock_framing._source: RI-CAM03 §B–§F; springs and boom ramp are [CMB06] and live in game/data/combat/lockon.json

modes._source: RI-CAM05 §F — closed vocabulary. Anything else in a trace is a fail.
modes.zoom_input: none — the wheel and every zoom axis are unbound for the gameplay camera

dialogue.accommodation_fires: once, at open — never on a topic change

menu.item_inspection: separate render target with its own camera; the world camera does not move

interior_architecture._source: RI-CAM05 §D — binding on the WORLD builder, measured by the camera

feel.head_bob: none — the pivot height is a constant

player_body._source: this piece — the world-collision radius the camera's floor arithmetic depends on
player_body.rationale: 0.55 m is what makes the penetration guard's worst case (back flat against a wall) land at arm 0.37 m with a camera-to-head distance of 0.386 m, which clears RI-CAM05 §F's 0.35 m invariant. A smaller body radius puts the camera inside the character's head in that pose; a larger one does not fit RI-CAM05 §D's 1.80 m doorway with comfortable clearance.
